This petition has been filed under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (corresponding to Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023) by the petitioners, seeking quashment of the criminal complaint and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom, pending before the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bhopal, in RCT No.9910853/2017 (Sangita Chouhan vs.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that a criminal complaint registered as RCT No.9910853/2017 was filed by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:863 2 MCRC-1809-2021 respondent/complainant under Section 200 Cr.P.C. against the petitioners,
alleging herself to be the wife of Petitioner No.1 and alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 406, 323, and 34 IPC.
Petitioner No.1 is alleged to be her husband, while Petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are his parents, and Petitioner Nos.4 and 5 are his sisters.

It is submitted that the learned Trial Court, without following the procedure prescribed under Section 202 Cr.P.C.,
mechanically took cognizance of the complaint and issued notices to the petitioners vide order dated 09.10.2018.

It is further submitted that the respondent suppressed the material fact of her previous subsisting marriage with Bhuvnesh Chouhan, rendering the alleged marriage with Petitioner No.1 null and void ab initio under the Hindu Marriage Act.

This position has been upheld by this Court in Criminal Revision No.725/2018 (Smt. Sangita Chouhan Vs. Jitendra Chouhan ), wherein it was held by order dated 23.01.2019 that the respondent is not the legally wedded wife of Jitendra Chouhan Jitendra Chouhan vs Sangita Chouhan on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122007896/
1 (Petitioner No.1 herein) and is therefore not entitled to maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C.,
1973.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the present complaint is a counterblast to FIR Crime No.227/2017 lodged by Petitioner No.1 against the respondent and her relatives under Sections 496, 417, 384, and 120-B IPC.
A charge-sheet was filed on 08.01.2018 against the respondent and other co-accused.

The respondent had also filed a petition for quashment of the charge-sheet [M.Cr.C. No.10199/2017 (Smt. Sangita Chouhan & others Vs. State of MP & others ), which was subsequently withdrawn.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:863 3 MCRC-1809-2021 application filed by the respondent under Section 125 Cr.P.C. was dismissed by Family Court as well as this Court, holding that the respondent was not the legally married wife of petitioner No.1.

It is further submitted that application filed under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bhopal, was allowed without proper discussion of the evidence and facts of the case, and Appellate Court merely affirmed the order without establishing that any domestic violence had taken place against the respondent.

sentences.text: Assailing the aforesaid orders, petitioners have filed Criminal Revision No.5531/2024 (Jitendra Chouhan & others Vs. Smt. Sangita Chouhan ), by order dated 16.07.2025, the aforesaid orders have been quashed by this Court.

sentences.text: It is therefore prayed that criminal complaint and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom against the petitioners may be quashed.
4 . It is a settled position of law that for an offence of cruelty under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code, the complainant must be the legally wedded wife of the accused-husband.

In the present case, the complainant/respondent, who already had a living spouse, could not have been the legally wedded wife of Petitioner No.1 without termination of her previous marriage by a decree of a competent court of law.
Thus, the alleged offence of cruelty against the petitioners is not at all maintainable at the instance of the respondent, who is not the legally wedded wife of Petitioner No.1.
5 The aforesaid legal position has been reiterated in series of judgments.

Worthy to mention is the decision delivered by the three Judges NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:863 4 MCRC-1809-2021 Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shivcharan Lal Verma vs.
State of M.P. reported in JT 2002(2)SC 641 , wherein it was held that- "For the offence u/s 498A IPC, it is essential that the complainant should be a legally wedded wife of the accused.

entities.text:
Shivcharan Lal Verma vs.
State of M.P. reported in JT 2002(2)SC 641
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That is to say that the marriage between accused and complainant should be a valid marriage according to the laws prevailing.

In the present case where the complainant herself dishonestly and fraudulently entered into illegal marriage which is void per-se, doesn't entitle her the character of wife as stipulated under Hindu Marriage Act."
Resultantly, for want of the legal character of a wife, the above- mentioned complaint case is not sustainable in light of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

Jitendra Chouhan vs Sangita Chouhan on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122007896/
2 6 .

Learned counsel for the State opposes the application considering the serious allegations under Sections 498-A, 406, 323 and 34 IPC, which disclose cruelty, physical assault and criminal breach of trust committed with common intention.
The accusations relate to dowry harassment and misappropriation of stridhan.
Grant of relief at this stage would adversely affect the investigation and may lead to tampering with evidence or influencing witnesses.
Hence, this petition/application deserves to be dismissed.
7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case record.

8 . Having heard learned counsel for the parties and upon perusal of the material on record, this Court finds that the respondent has been held not to be the legally wedded wife of petitioner No.1 by a competent court,
and such finding has attained finality.

In view of the settled legal position that a complaint under Section 498-A IPC is not maintainable at the instance of a NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:863 5 MCRC-1809-2021 woman who is not a legally wedded wife, continuation of the criminal proceedings would amount to abuse of the process of law.
9 . In view of overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of considered opinion that continuation of criminal proceedings would serve no useful purpose.

Accordingly, criminal complaint and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom, pending before the Court of the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bhopal, in RCT No.9910853/2017 (Sangita Chouhan vs. Jitendra Chouhan & Others), in respect of offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 406, 323 and 34 of Indian Penal Code are hereby quashed qua the petitioners.
